title: Concept: Unchecked type reinterpretation via transmute in rust — review required
description: In rust, memory is reinterpreted without a check. Rust relies on type invariants for safety, and transmute is the explicit escape hatch that can violate them: an invalid enum discriminant or a misaligned reference produces undefined behaviour rather than a panic. The call compiles whenever the sizes match, so the mistake is invisible until it is exploited or fuzzed.
applicability: rust crates that parse binary formats or optimise hot paths.
risk: Undefined behaviour and memory-safety violations; MEDIUM severity.
